pageTitle: Feature Store Mini — batch feature workflow
title: Feature Store Mini
summary: A small batch pipeline: raw customer table in, one build step, validated feature table out. Definitions and transforms live in code so the CLI and the HTTP API run the same logic.
metaDescription: Batch feature pipeline with a shared definition registry, pandas transforms, validation checks, FastAPI catalog and transform endpoint, and pytest CI.
limitations: Not an online feature store: no point-in-time joins, no real-time serving layer, no Feast/Tecton-scale materialization.
Scope is a single-repo pattern for consistent offline features and reviewable validation—not training or model hosting.
Demo raw schema is Telco-style tabular data; production would swap the same pattern for your own column contract.

recruiter.eyebrow: Proof of work · batch ML data discipline
recruiter.summary: Production-minded pattern: one registry for feature meaning, one build path, structured validation, and the same transforms whether you run a CLI job or POST a CSV to FastAPI.
recruiter.heroNote: Same code path in CLI and API; errors use stable codes (e.g. missing raw columns). OpenAPI documents the live service.

commercial.summary: Turn an agreed raw export into a model-ready feature table with named transforms and checks—useful for pilots where spreadsheets and ad-hoc scripts drift apart.
commercial.heroNote: Scoped pilot pattern—not SaaS or a full data platform. OpenAPI supports technical diligence; the outcome is a repeatable table, not novelty UI.
commercial.pageTitle: Feature Store Mini — pilot feature-prep pattern
commercial.metaDescription: Pilot-sized pattern: turn agreed operational exports into validated, model-ready feature tables with one build path—honest scope, no enterprise feature-store claims.
limitations: Not enterprise feature-store software: no Feast/Tecton-scale materialization, no real-time serving layer, and not a hosted multi-tenant product.
A single-repo implementation pattern for offline, batch features—not model training, scoring productization, or org-wide data governance.
Illustrative flows use Telco-style tabular data; your pilot pins the same idea to your own columns and approvals.
